name: DFW 2016 to 2020, 2015 IRC
description: Two-story slab house permitted September 2016 to 2020 under the 2015 IRC, still the Texas code and still Fort Worth's. Values follow the DOE Texas field study of 2015-code homes where it measured them. Many post-2020 DFW houses outside Dallas and Arlington were built to this code too. Inspect and override.

era.code_basis: 2015 IRC Chapter 11 statewide from September 1, 2016 (House Bill 1736; SECO); NCTCOG 4 ACH50 tradeoff available in DFW from 2017.

sources.citation: RhoeFlow DFW era template research (claude/01-plan/dfw-era-template-research.md), section Era by era: September 2016 to 2020. Every value, its range, evidence type and confidence.
Texas SECO, single-family energy code history: no statewide code before September 2001; 2000 IECC 2001-2011; 2009 IRC from 2012; 2015 IRC from September 2016

DOE/PNNL Texas Field Study final report (2022), Phase III 2015 IRC homes in climate zone 2A: mean 4.3 ACH50, total duct leakage 3.7 cfm25 per 100 ft2, ceiling R-32.5 (43% met R-38), window U 0.35 and SHGC 0.22, attic ducts R-6.2

2015 IECC Chapter 4 (Texas code via 2015 IRC Chapter 11 from Sept 1, 2016), climate zone 3: U 0.35, SHGC 0.25, ceiling R-38, wall R-20 or 13+5, 3 ACH50, attic ducts R-8 (3 in. and up), total duct leakage 4 cfm25 per 100 ft2
NCTCOG 4 ACH50 tradeoff for 2015-code single-family homes (from Jan 31, 2017): R-49 ceiling, wall R-13+3, U 0.32; R-6 ducts allowed with a radiant barrier

ceiling_insulation_cavity_r.basis: Texas field study measured a mean R-32.5 and only 43% met the code R-38, so the pick is R-30; NCTCOG tradeoff homes have R-49. Measure the depth and override.

wall_insulation_cavity_r.basis: Code: R-20 cavity or R-13 plus R-5 continuous. The Houston field study saw R-13 walls, which is the zone 2 code, so it does not apply here.

air_leakage.basis: Texas field study measured a mean 4.3 ACH50, rounded to the poor side; code 3, DFW tradeoff 4. A blower-door result replaces this.

duct_insulation_r.basis: Texas field study measured R-6.2 attic ducts (code R-8 for ducts 3 in. and up). Read the jacket label.

duct_leakage_to_outside.basis: Code total leakage limit 4 cfm25 per 100 ft2 (field mean 3.7), which caps leakage to outside. A duct-blaster result replaces this.

roof_radiant_barrier.basis: Assumption: no prevalence data was found; the NCTCOG tradeoff's R-6 duct option requires one. Confirm from the attic photo.
